title: Notice of Intent - BPA for Language Services
description: This Notice is not a call for sources, quotes, or solicitations. The deadline for response is 1700 EDT on October 3, 2026. Responses may be directed by e-mail to Angelika Graham, Contracting Officer, Office of Language Services, Department of State. Any technical or other information received in response to this Notice will be considered for the sole purpose of market research for future requirements. The Office of Language Services of the U.S. Department of State contracts directly with qualified individuals to provide foreign language interpreting, translating, and related services in support of diplomatic and foreign affairs activities at the highest levels of the U.S. Government. The Office has limited contracting authority pursuant to Department of State Acquisition Regulations (DOSAR), the Foreign Affairs Manual (FAM), and FAR Part 13 to contract for interpreters and translators domestically. DOSAR 601.601-70 further defines this as the authority �to enter into and administer simplified acquisition transactions under FAR Part 13 and orders against existing contracts up to the maximum ordering threshold or limitation for interpreting, translating, conference reporting, and related language support and escort services.� The Office establishes fixed rates of payment for specific language services each fiscal year on the basis of market research. In accordance with industry standards, these rates are not published for the general public. For the purposes of this Notice, the term �qualified� describes those individuals who have passed the Office of Language Services test(s) of interpreting and translating skill for one or more foreign languages and have successfully provided language services under a Blanket Purchase Agreement or Purchase Order with the Office of Language Services in the past. In accordance with 6 FAM 1550, the Office develops and administers examinations to evaluate the interpreting and translating skills of prospective direct-hire and contract staff. These exams are offered by invitation only subject to the needs of the Department. Individual members of the public who wish to be considered as test candidates should visit https://www.state.gov/freelance-linguists-ols/ to view criteria and application information. In addition, qualified bidders must hold U.S. citizenship or permanent resident status and have active contractor profiles in the System for Award Management (SAM). They must also be able to obtain and maintain a Moderate or High-risk Public Trust Certification from the State Department�s Office of Personnel Suitability and Security. They must agree to accept our fixed rates of payment for specific language services. Finally, they are forbidden from subcontracting and must adhere to strict professional standards. The Office of Language Services intends to issue Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) for Language Services to qualified bidders effective October 1, 2026. The Office anticipates that roughly 850 Agreements with individual foreign language translators, interpreters, and specialists will be issued. The value of calls against these individual Agreements will not exceed $350,000, with no individual call to exceed $25,000 and over half of all calls at or below the micro purchase threshold $15,000. There is no guarantee of assignment under these Agreements. The anticipated total combined annual value of all calls against all of these Agreements is between $20 million and $30 million. Individual BPA calls are awarded at the discretion of the Language Services Contracting Officer, based on recommendations from Subject Matter Experts within the Office and factors including evaluated skill sets, prior performance, and availability to accept the assignment.

description: La fiabilisation de la station de pompage interdépartementale VL2 située à Villeneuve Saint Georges appartenant au Syndicat Interdépartemental pour l'Assainissement de l'Agglomération Parisienne et exploitée par le conseil départemental du Val de Marne (Direction des Services de l'Environnement et de l'Assainissement). La station de relevage VL2 a été construite en 1991 afin d'alimenter la STEP de Valenton (Seine amont - SAM) avec les effluents collectés dans le Val de Marne et pour soulager ainsi Seine aval. Le présent projet consiste à mettre en application les résultats de l'étude de fiabilisation hydraulique et de l'AMDEC réalisées de 2016 à 2018 pour tout ce qui était noté en criticité inacceptable de degré 1, à savoir : - Modification du pompage permettant de garantir en continu les consignes de débits de la STEP quelques soient les occurrences de défaut des pompes, - Sécurisation de la bâche de refoulement, - Cloisonnement des TGBT et transformateurs, - Modification du système de dégrillage pour évacuer les broyats, - Changement des vannes d'entrées de poste. Les objectifs sont triples : - D'une part, garantir une disponibilité et le secours du pompage de VL2 en adéquation avec les objectifs épuratoires de SAM (débit de 6m3/s) et ainsi diminuer les routages vers SESAME et Charenton - D'autre part, fiabiliser les équipements de la station VL2 dont l'analyse des modes de défaillances (AMDEC) a mis en évidence une criticité inacceptable, - Enfin, améliorer la qualité de l'effluent relevé vers l'usine de Valenton en supprimant les refus de dégrillage à la source (volonté partagée sur la zone SIAAP pour diminuer l'ensablement du prétraitement et améliorer ainsi l'efficacité de la station d'épuration)

title: Dynamic Mechanical Analyzer (DMA)
description: Dynamic Mechanical Analyzer (DMA) South-Eastern Finland University of Applied Sciences (Xamk) is purchasing a Dynamic Mechanical Analyzer (DMA) system according to this tender documentation. The equipment will be located at the Mikpolis RDI unit in Mikkeli, Finland. Pricing must include shipping costs to Mikkeli, Finland (Patteristonkatu 3, 50100 Mikkeli, Finland). Installation, commissioning and user training must be included in the delivery. The primary use of the equipment is the characterization of the viscoelastic and mechanical properties of materials as a function of temperature, frequency, time and applied force or deformation. The system will be used for determining properties such as storage and loss modulus, damping behaviour, creep and stress relaxation behaviour, and characteristic transition temperatures. The equipment must be suitable for a wide range of materials, including polymers, polymer composites, elastomers and biomaterials. The system must support several deformation modes, including tensile, compression and bending measurements. The DMA system must provide accurate force and displacement measurement over a wide dynamic range and enable measurements over a broad temperature and frequency range. The system must include controlled heating and cooling as well as the possibility to perform measurements under a controlled purge-gas atmosphere. The system must support both dynamic and static mechanical testing. Dynamic measurement modes must include temperature, frequency, combined temperature-frequency, load and time sweeps. Static measurement capabilities must include creep, stress relaxation and universal testing. The system must include the sample holders and accessories required for three-point bending, single and dual cantilever bending, tensile, compression and penetration measurements. The equipment must include software for instrument control, measurement execution, real-time monitoring, calibration, data acquisition and analysis. Simultaneous measurement and evaluation must be possible. The software must provide tools for determining characteristic temperatures and values and for exporting measurement data and graphical results in commonly used formats. Xamk currently operates NETZSCH DMA, DSC and TGA instruments. To maintain compatibility with the existing laboratory data and analysis workflow, the analysis software supplied with the new DMA system must be capable of opening and evaluating measurement data generated by the existing DSC and TGA systems. Compatibility with the existing measurement data is considered essential in order to enable combined analysis of DMA, DSC and TGA results and to avoid separate software environments for the different thermal analysis techniques. The system must include the necessary calibration functions and calibration materials for verification of the force, dynamic response, system compliance, phase and temperature measurement. The calibration procedures should be integrated into the instrument software. The equipment will be used in a multi-user research and testing laboratory environment. Therefore, reliable operation, reproducible measurement conditions, ease of use, efficient changing of measurement geometries, traceability of measurement configurations and availability of technical support are important. The offered solution must comprise a complete and operational DMA system including the instrument, temperature-control systems, sample holders, calibration accessories, measurement and analysis software, computer equipment required for operation, installation, commissioning and user training. A budget of EUR 130 000 (0% VAT) has been allocated for this procurement. XAMK will not accept offers exceeding this amount.,

Il comprend entre autres les capacités suivantes : • Monitoring des infrastructures et des composants techniques associés, notamment les serveurs, systèmes d’exploitation, conteneurs, bases de données, middlewares, composants réseau liés aux applications, files de messages, API et plateformes d’intégration. • Monitoring des applications et des transactions de bout en bout, avec des capacités de détection des anomalies, de diagnostic accéléré, d’analyse des dépendances et d’identification des causes racines. • Monitoring de l’expérience utilisateur, tant réelle que synthétique, pour les applications et les parcours utilisateurs critiques. • Collecte, centralisation, normalisation, corrélation et exploitation des données de télémétrie, incluant les métriques, événements, logs et traces. • Mise à disposition de tableaux de bord adaptés aux différents rôles et niveaux de responsabilité, notamment la direction, les opérations IT, les équipes applicatives, le NOC/support et les responsables d’applications et de services. • Définition, mesure et suivi des indicateurs de niveau de service, notamment les SLI/SLO, les golden signals et les error budgets, ainsi que les mécanismes d’alerte associés. • Intégration avec les outils et processus ITSM existants, notamment pour la gestion des incidents, des problèmes, des changements, des escalades, du reporting et des revues de service. • Mise en place de mécanismes d’alerting intelligents, permettant la réduction du bruit, la corrélation des alertes, leur priorisation en fonction de l’impact métier et leur routage vers les équipes responsables. • Analyse de l’impact sur les services IT et les services métier critiques, sur la base des dépendances entre les utilisateurs, les applications, les composants techniques et les services concernés. Le but du marché est de conclure un Accord-Cadre en cascade avec tous les Soumissionnaires qui auront remis une offre conforme. Le Soumissionnaire le mieux classé suivant les critères d’attribution sera considéré comme Adjudicataire actif. Les autres Soumissionnaires dont l’offre est conforme seront considérés comme Adjudicataire de réserve. Leur contrat sera activé en cas de défaillance de l’opérateur actif (cascade). De plus Sibelga se réserve le droit de contractualiser les licences en direct avec le fournisseur du framework retenu.

Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/minerva-initiative-uncrewed-air-system-cargomunition-drop?auHash=aUYSwVfmHbX1C0Ib4yBClo29RgX8gchivNFIqzsBK8s Challenge title: MINERVA Initiative – Uncrewed Air System for Cargo/Munition Drop Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) requires an uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) for the aerial delivery of cargo and munitions that is domestically produced, easy to operate and maintain, and adequately rugged to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: August 24, 2026 Closing date: October 5, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement The CA soldier will face an increasingly complex and dangerous battlespace in the future. A major element of the complexity and danger is the proliferation of multi-spectral sensors and precision weapons that will limit the CA’s ability to move cargo and strike enemy targets at range by using attributable ballistic trajectory weapons without the risk of being targeted and attacked. The CA presently lacks an UAS capable of conducting short-range cargo delivery of light supplies or remote munitions drops. The CA requires an innovative uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) that provides an uncrewed alternative to move combat supplies forward towards the frontline and to deliver munitions independent of predictable ballistic trajectories and launch signatures. This innovation must be simple, durable, and highly survivable, providing soldiers with an effective capability for future conflicts that integrates seamlessly into operations while minimizing training and maintenance requirements, allowing soldiers to focus on their mission. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution would: 1. Be composed of an: a. Air vehicle: The airframe containing the onboard electronics, propulsion, and payload. b. Sensor payload: The equipment required for navigation and to complete a mission, such as cameras or imaging systems. c. Ground control station (GCS): The system (laptop, tablet, or handheld controller) used by the human operator to control flight and manage missions. d. Radio: The wireless system that connects the GCS to the UAS to transmit commands and receive telemetry/data. e. Battery with charger: A battery for the UAS and a battery charger capable of charging multiple batteries simultaneously. f. Remote antenna: An external antenna placed 100m away from the GCS to enhance signal strength, reduce interference, and extend operational range. 2. Operate in various weather conditions, including at a minimum: a. temperature range of -20°C and +40°C; b. minimum windspeed of up to 40 km/hr; and c. light rain or snow ranging 0.5mm/m²/hr. 3. Be able to carry a minimum payload of 5kg of cargo. 4. Have a maximum takeoff weight than 25kg (includes payload). 5. Have both a minimum operational radius of 10km and an endurance of 30 min in continuous movement while carrying its payload. 6. Have vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) capability in a maximum area of 2m². 7. Be stowable in a 70-litre pack. 8. Be capable of operating at a minimum operational altitude of 1000 feet Above Ground Level (AGL). Additional outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Be deployable from a stowed state to a mission-ready state in 10 minutes or less. This includes the completion of all pre-mission preparation activities, including but not limited to unloading vehicle, loading/fueling the power system and loading/configuring mission set resulting in a vehicle that is fully mission-ready at the line of departure. 2. Have a sensor that enables the operator to recognize a target at a minimum distance under the following conditions: a. Day – Person (180cm) at 0.5km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 1km b. Night – Person (180cm) at 0.25km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 0.5km 3. Emit no more than 5 decibels Sound Pressure Level (dB SPL) of noise in all frequency ranges, measured at a 500m distance from the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). 4. Be capable of operating with fibre-optic wire, or an alternate non-Electromagnetic (EM) spectrum means. 5. Incorporate Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) 256k encryption or equivalent for data transmission security. 6. Return to a pre-determined location, hover/loiter and/or climb in case of loss of link. 7. Have an aggregated projected production cost of $40,000 CAD or less per system. 8. Have a Ground Control Station (GCS) that: a. Incorporates a training simulation capability for Mission Planning. b. Has a minimum remote antenna cable length of 50m. c. Enables UAS navigation via both direct operator control and autonomously using waypoint navigation via the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). d. Displays the following information: - Location of vehicle in 6 figure Military Grid Reference System (MGRS); - Orientation of vehicle (pitch/roll/yaw); - Point of aim of camera in 6 figure MGRS; - Real-time full motion video feed; - Altitude in Metres above Sea Level (MSL); and - Battery life. e. Is capable of interfacing with the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK) battle management system to push UAS Position Location Information (PLI) and target PLI. 9. Have an alternate non-electric or hybrid power system capable of sustained operation beyond battery power (i.e. a gas-powered system or a gas/electric hybrid power system). 10. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies . To achieve this, Offerors are requested to provide as an attachment to their proposal, a list identifying the solution's critical components, the country of production and sourcing for each component. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to replace an existing hydro utility pole and associated 44 kV air break switch located on the primary electrical feed to Beaver Creek Institution. title: Norway – Software-related services – Electronic substance register
description: Background Trøndelag county needs a modern and comprehensive system for electronic substance register, which can support the entity's work on health, safety and the environment. The procurement is being carried out in order to ensure easy access to updated chemical information, contribute to compliance with the current regulations and facilitate safe handling of chemical products throughout the entire organisation. The county has a compound entity with different user groups and work areas, including sixth form colleges, laboratories, operation and cleaning functions, workshops, dental health services, road operation, administration and teaching environments. This sets requirements for a system that is user friendly, accessible and suitable for both employees and pupils, while at the same time being managed in an efficient way across units and professional environments. The aim of the procurement is to establish a joint system that provides a better overview of chemicals, supports local needs and at the same time enables central management and follow-up. Tenderers must therefore understand that the system shall function in a large and varied organisation, with a need for both broad availability and appropriate administration. Description of the assignment Trøndelag county shall procure an electronic substance register that is delivered as a site license for approx. 5,000 employees and 20,000 students. The system shall cover the county ́s need for registration, disclosure and management of information on chemical products across the entity. The delivery includes a digital system with functionality for i.a. search and access to safety data sheets, an overview of chemicals, as well as support for the accompanying HSE work such as risk assessment, substitute and exposure register. The system shall be suitable for different types of users and it can be used in both teaching related and operational contexts. Furthermore, the system shall support secure and efficient access management, including log-on and user administration adapted to the county ́s established identity management. A system is requested that combines user friendliness for local units with the possibility for general administration and control across the organisation. The design of the tender Tenderers shall fill in and respond to all points in the ESPD form, requirement specifications and price form. Any documentation beyond replies directly to the requirement specification shall be uploaded as pdf files, unless otherwise specified. The following shall be completed and submitted with the tender: · Complete Annex 1 - Tender Form · Digital requirement specifications and price form with reference to any annexes. · Completed data processing agreement with annexes. · Censured version of the offer

description: Le présent marché constitue un accord-cadre mono-attributaire au sens de la réglementation relative aux marchés publics. Il fixe les conditions applicables aux prestations récurrentes ainsi qu’aux prestations et développements complémentaires qui pourront être commandés au fur et à mesure des besoins du pouvoir adjudicateur pendant sa durée. L’accord-cadre a pour objet la fourniture, la mise en oeuvre, la maintenance, le support et l’évolution d’un système intégré de gestion des ressources humaines, couvrant notamment : • la gestion complète de la paie des agents contractuels, statutaires, mandataires, bénévoles et rentiers (y compris gestion des primes, des absences, des interruptions de carrière, des jetons de présence, des déclarations fiscales et sociales, etc.) ; • la gestion du temps et des présences, incluant les badgeages, la validation des congés, l’encodage et la validation du télétravail, la gestion des missions, la planification, ainsi que l’accès agent via portail web et application mobile. Le marché vise à garantir une cohérence fonctionnelle et technique complète entre ces deux domaines, dans une approche unique et intégrée. Il ne comprend pas la fourniture des terminaux physiques de badgeage. Le pouvoir adjudicateur en dispose déjà. Les soumissionnaires devront s’assurer de la comptabilité de leur solution avec l’usage des pointeuses actuelles (voir annexe E). Le marché sera conclu pour une durée maximale de 10 ans. La durée de ce marché s’explique par les investissements et développements nécessaires pour la mise à disposition d’une solution répondant aux besoins et contraintes d’HYGEA.

L’accord-cadre a pour objet la fourniture, la mise en oeuvre, la maintenance, le support et l’évolution d’un système intégré de gestion des ressources humaines, couvrant notamment : • la gestion complète de la paie des agents contractuels, statutaires, mandataires, bénévoles et rentiers (y compris gestion des primes, des absences, des interruptions de carrière, des jetons de présence, des déclarations fiscales et sociales, etc.) ; • la gestion du temps et des présences, incluant les badgeages, la validation des congés, l’encodage et la validation du télétravail, la gestion des missions, la planification, ainsi que l’accès agent via portail web et application mobile. Le marché vise à garantir une cohérence fonctionnelle et technique complète entre ces deux domaines, dans une approche unique et intégrée. Il ne comprend pas la fourniture des terminaux physiques de badgeage. Le pouvoir adjudicateur en dispose déjà. Les soumissionnaires devront s’assurer de la comptabilité de leur solution avec l’usage des pointeuses actuelles (voir annexe E). Le marché sera conclu pour une durée maximale de 10 ans. La durée de ce marché s’explique par les investissements et développements nécessaires pour la mise à disposition d’une solution répondant aux besoins et contraintes d’HYGEA.

title: Letter of Interest / Advance Notice to Industry Multidisciplinary Environmental Services RFSO
description: AMENDMENT 02 – PUBLICATION OF THE PRESENTATION AND QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS (Q&A) FROM THE PRE-TENDER INFORMATION SESSION HELD ON SEPTEMBER 22, 2026 This published notice is not a solicitation. This document does not offer any commitments with respect to future purchases or contracts. The information in this notice is illustrative and may be revised as circumstances change. The purpose of this notice is to inform industry that Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC) intends to establish new Departmental Individual Standing Offers (DISOs) to replace the expiring DISOs under EW699-220114 Multidisciplinary Environmental Services. The new DISOs will include the following consulting services for PWGSC’s Western Region: • Environmental impact assessments, permitting and studies o Environmental impact assessment o Permitting and regulatory support o Biological studies and investigations o Archaeological assessment • Environmental management of federal facilities o Environmental management and compliance o Hazardous building materials surveys o Air quality o Potable water sampling o Storage tank system audits • Contaminated sites consulting services o Phase I, II, III environmental site assessments (ESAs) o Geotechnical assessment o Human health and ecological risk assessment o Climate change risk assessment o Remedial options analyses /Evaluation and remedial action / Risk management action plans • Remediation planning, tender support, and supervision o Remediation planning o Site supervision and contract administration services o Cost estimating PWGSC plans to develop the upcoming multidisciplinary environmental services Request for Standing Offers (RFSOs) with the following structure: Publish four RFSOs on the CanadaBuys tender opportunities website, each aligned to a distinct geographic area and supplier eligibility requirements: 1. Prairies RFSO: Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba 2. Prairies PSIB RFSO: Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba, limited to Indigenous suppliers in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) 3. Northwest RFSO: Northwest Territories 4. Nunavut RFSO: Nunavut Settlement Area, limited to Inuit firms registered on the Inuit Firm Registry Each RFSO will allow consultant firms to qualify for a DISO for the geographic area covered by that RFSO. ? Consultants may submit offers under more than one RFSO. ? Call-up distribution within each standing offer will be based on pre-determined percentages. ? Each standing offer will include two tiers, with separate call-up procedures as follows: 1. For requirements up to $100,000 (including applicable taxes), PWGSC may either: i. issue the call-up to the next firm on the rotation (rotational call-ups), ii. select the Offeror of their choice (selective call-ups) iii. compete the call-up on the basis of a work plan, level of effort, cost of disbursements and/or travel or Indigenous/Inuit commitments (competitive call-ups). 2. For requirements above $100,000 (including applicable taxes), PWGSC may either: i. issue the call-up to the next firm on the rotation (rotational call-ups), ii. direct a call-up to a firm with ‘best-fit’ justification (‘best fit’ call-ups), or iii. compete the call-up on the basis of a work plan, level of effort, cost of disbursements and/or travel or Indigenous/Inuit commitments (competitive call-ups /the pre-established unit rates of the standing offers will be respected). Each issued call-up will affect the order of priority of rotational call-ups to attain the ideal business volume distribution. Modern Treaties/Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs) Many of the multidisciplinary environmental services tool call-ups will be subject to modern treaties/CLCAs, which define the land and resource rights of Indigenous signatories and are intended to improve the social, cultural, political and economic well-being of the concerned Indigenous peoples. Accordingly, the RFSOs will include socio-economic benefits criteria designed to maximize opportunities for Indigenous businesses, labour, subcontracting and training. The Nunavut stream in particular will be exclusive to firms listed in the Inuit Firm Registry [https://inuitfirm.tunngavik.com]. Vendor Performance Management PWGSC will develop a vendor performance mechanism that is specific to the standing offers. The mechanism is designed to adjust the percentage distribution of call-ups according to the performance of each offeror. Buy Canadian Policy As part of the Government of Canada’s Buy Canadian Procurement Policy, the Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurements will apply to the RFSOs. Where applicable, each RFSO will include the required clauses and certifications. Optional Pre-Tender Information Session An information session will be held through a Microsoft Teams videoconference meeting on September 22, 2026. The session will begin at 10:00 AM Mountain Daylight Time. If you wish to participate in the information session. To facilitate networking, partnership opportunities, and future business relationships among suppliers interested in multidisciplinary environmental services, we invite interested participants to complete the form below. Information submitted through the form may be shared with other interested suppliers and may be published online to support industry engagement and collaboration. https://forms-formulaires.alpha.canada.ca/en/id/cmu44qeqe00x501ypgzcgifpn

title: Injectable Egg-Free Influenza Vaccine 2027
description: The Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support is soliciting for the supply of Injectable Egg-Free Influenza Vaccine for the 2027-2028 flu season. Approximately 300,000 doses are included in this requirement. (Quantities may increase or decrease pending receipt of final Service requirements.) The vaccines shall be in prefilled syringes presentation. The vaccine shall be FDA-approved for immunizing individuals 18 years and older. The formula for the 2027-2028 season shall be determined by the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee. Other specification data is included in the solicitation. Successful contractor must have FDA Approval, and the vaccine must be U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommended. National Stock Numbers shall be established at the time of award. An indefinite quantity contract is proposed. The quantity indicated is an annual estimate only. The guaranteed minimum will be 75% of the annual estimate, and a contract maximum will be established at 150% of the annual estimate. Ordered quantities shall be delivered to the Defense Depot New Cumberland, PA. The contractor shall be capable of delivering 40% of the requirement by August 12, 2027, 25% by August 26, 2027, 25% by September 9, 2027, and the residual 10% by September 23, 2027. The Delivery Schedule shall apply to the estimated annual quantity. This delivery schedule is the preferred delivery schedule. Other delivery schedules may be considered. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and SAM.gov at https://www.sam.gov. Interested parties should contact Rosbert Jones (445-737-1254) (Rosbert.Jones@dla.mil) for any questions/comments. Interested parties are further advised to set up automated notifications of presolicitation or solicitation changes through this website. The current projected solicitation date is October of 2026. DLA reserves the right to issue the solicitation before or after the projected solicitation date.

title: 58--OLES LONG RANGE MWIR THERMAL BINOCULARS
description: The Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management (BLM), intends to award a sole-source contract to Teledyne FLIR for three Recon HD high-definition, dual-sensor long-range thermal binocular/camera systems with 2� doubler lenses. BLM Law Enforcement currently utilizes legacy Teledyne FLIR Recon long-range, cooled mid-wave infrared (MWIR) thermal systems in remote and austere environments. These systems support law-enforcement missions including suspect detection and identification, detection of small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS), operational overwatch, search-and-rescue, evidence collection, and reconnaissance. The requirement is for a Section 889-compliant, long-range, lightweight thermal system that integrates a low-light visible camera with a cooled MWIR imager and provides a high-definition 1280 � 720 thermal sensor, High Operating Temperature (HOT) MWIR cryo-cooled focal plane array, 8-micron pixel pitch, and 2� doubler lens. The Recon HD also provides long-range detection capabilities, including specified vehicle detection to 9,700 meters and human detection to 3,900 meters. Based on market research, BLM has identified the Teledyne FLIR Recon HD as the only Section 889-compliant solution that meets BLM's requirements for a long-range, high-definition, cooled MWIR thermal binocular/camera system and interfaces with existing field equipment. BLM intends to pursue this acquisition on a sole-source basis under the authority applicable to only one source being reasonably available. Response to Notice All responsible sources may submit a quotation or capability information demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's requirement, which will be considered by the agency. Responses shall be submitted electronically before the end of this announcement period. The Government will consider information received in determining whether a competitive procurement is appropriate.

title: MABSM Sustainment & Implementation Services Sources Sought
description: CLARIFICATION REGARDING AUTHORIZED DISTRIBUTOR LETTERS The Government has received questions regarding the requirement to provide "authorized distributor letters" under Section F of the Sources Sought. The Government clarifies the following: Authorized distributor letters are only required for respondents whose proposed solutions include physical hardware, IT equipment, or commercial software licenses. Respondents proposing purely professional services, customized solutions, or approaches that do not involve non-manufactured items, commercial software, or hardware are not required to submit these letters. The omission of authorized distributor letters by services-only respondents will have no impact on the evaluation of capability or the compliance of the submission. All other instructions and the response deadline of 08 October 2026 remain unchanged. Notice: This is not a solicitation but rather a Sources Sought Synopsis to determine potential sources for information and planning purposes only. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if responsible sources exist, to assist in determining if this effort can be competitive and/or a total Small Business Set-Aside. PLEASE SEE ADDITIONAL ATTACHMENTS FOR FURTHER DETAILS AND VENDOR CAPABILITY QUESTIONS Program Details: The MABSM application is a highly customized, mission-critical Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) system. Originally built on a baseline commercial Impresa MRO/ERP software foundation, the system has undergone extensive, continuous customization over the past 24 years. To date, the MABSM baseline includes over 242,000 custom code changes, program specifications, testing criteria, and complex interface logic. These modifications enable real-time communication with 17 legacy Department of Defense (DoD) systems. This highly specialized, proprietary configuration of the COTS software bears little structural resemblance to its commercial progenitor and operates as a unique hybrid system. MABSM operates and is sustained within the Department of the Air Force's Cloud 1 enterprise cloud environment, leveraging DoD Impact Level 4/5 (IL4/IL5) secure cloud infrastructure. Sourcing specialized contractors who can operate seamlessly within Cloud 1's DevSecOps frameworks, managed services, and security boundaries is crucial to system stability. MABSM dictates the real-time tracking of critical assets, including aircraft parts, financial transactions, and Nuclear Weapons-Related Material (NWRM) items. Due to the high-tempo depot environments in which it is deployed, the system requires a performance baseline exceeding 95% system uptime and near-zero code degradation. Furthermore, national security mandates dictate 100% real-time accountability of NWRM items within any given 24-hour period. title: Belgium – Human resources management consultancy services – Feedback à 360°
description: Cet accord-cadre a pour but de désigner un partenaire qui permettra à des responsables d'équipe de recevoir, via un outil web, du feedback de la part de leur propre responsable d'équipe, des membres de leur équipe et/ou de leurs collègues/pairs. Par « feedback à 360° », on entend : un processus de feedback structuré dans lequel un responsable d'équipe reçoit du feedback sur base de son auto-évaluation, mais aussi du feedback de son propre responsable d'équipe, des membres de son équipe et de ses pairs. C’est la Loterie Nationale qui détermine quels groupes de répondants sont interrogés par cycle de feedback. Voir documents du marché à télécharger sur la plateforme e-Procurement. La sélection des candidats s’effectuera sur la base du présent guide de sélection (phase 1). Seuls les candidats sélectionnés seront invités à soumettre une offre (phase 2). Les documents du marché de la phase 2 sont mis à disposition à titre informatif. La date ultime mentionnée est la date de clôture pour l’introduction uniquement des demandes de participation (dossiers de candidatures). Ceci signifie que c’est uniquement votre réponse pour la PHASE 1 (phase de sélection) qui doit être introduite sur e-Procurement. Les éventuelles questions/réponses et rectifications seront également publiées et mises à disposition sur ce même site web. Veuillez donc consulter régulièrement le présent avis de marché. Personne de contact: Olivier Marchettini (olivier.marchettini@loterie-nationale.be)

title: ZAMBIA - Specific Procurement Notice for procurement of a Human Resource Recruitment Firm
description: SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE Lusaka, Zambia 11 September 2026 Procurement of a Human Resource Recruitment Firm Ref: MCAZII-26-4005 The United States of America, acting through the Millennium Challenge Corporation (�MCC�) and the Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) (the �Government�) signed a Compact on 17th October 2024 to facilitate poverty reduction through economic growth in Zambia (the �Compact�) in the amount of Four Hundred and Fifty-Eight Million United States Dollars (US$ 458 million) (�MCC Funding�). The Compact also includes an additional US$ 33.75 million from the Government (the �Country Contribution�), bringing the total Compact proposed investment to US$ 491.75 million. The Compact program consists of four Projects: (1) the Roads and Access Project; (2) the Asset Finance Project; (3) the Agriculture Policy Reform and Institutional Strengthening Project; and (4) the American Catalyst Facility for Development (ACFD) Project. The Government has designated Millennium Challenge Account � Zambia II (�MCA-Zambia II�) to manage the implementation of the Activities, including entering into and managing the Government Service Provider Contracts. MCA-Zambia II now intends to apply a part of the proceeds of the Compact Funding to payments for contracts for goods, works and services. MCA-Zambia II is seeking to engage the services of a Human Resource Recruitment Firm to manage the recruitment process to hire qualified individuals for 52 positions. More details on these services are provided in the Terms of Reference in Section V of the Request for Offers (RFO). This RFO is open to all eligible entities (�Offerors�) who wish to respond. Subject to restrictions noted in the RFO, Offerors may associate with other Offerors to enhance their capacity to successfully carry out the assignment. A Human Resource Recruitment Firm will be selected under the Consultants Qualifications Selection (�CQS�) method, an evaluation procedure that is described in Section III of the RFO in accordance with the �MCC Accountable Entity Procurement Policy and Guidelines� provided on the MCC website www.mcc.gov/ppg. title: BEYOND Phase 2
description: Amendment 0002 is hereby issued to extend the proposal due date of the SIR to October 9, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0002. Questions and Answers are forthcoming. __________________________________________________ Amendment 0001 is hereby issued to extend the proposal due date of the SIR to September 25, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0001. __________________________________________________ This is the Screening Information Request (SIR) 697DCK-26-R-00423 for the BEYOND Phase 2 Selection. This procurement is in support of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Office (AUS). The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (P.L.118-63) Section 920 allows for the expansion of the BEYOND program. The FAA will implement a BEYOND Phase 2 competitive selection process, through this SIR. This competitive selection process is not a procurement or acquisition under the FAA Acquisition Management System. The FAA did not develop any acquisition requirements for this competitive selection process, and the process will not result in the award of a procurement contract. Consistent with the FAA Administrator�s authorities under 49 U.S.C. �106(l) and (m), this process will result in the award of an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). The FAA intends to award up to eight (8) OTAs through this solicitation. BEYOND Phase 2 has four programmatic focus areas: infrastructure, scalability, safety and automation. Five operational focus areas have also been identified as the greatest challenges that will need to be addressed for progress to be made: public safety, controlled airspace, remote, rural areas with inadequate infrastructure, on-airport operations and cross international borders. This SIR is seeking Offerors who can deliver successful outcomesin support of the BEYOND Phase 2 focus areas. See SIR for details. The FAA intends to competitively award up to eight (8) Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) with SLTTs in accordance with the SIR. The FAA reserves the right to execute additional OTAs if resources permit (49 U.S.C. � 106(l)). The Government will make OTA awards to the Offeror�s determined to best meet the selection criteria which are included in this SIR and reflected in the evaluation of the proposals. To be considered for award of this requirement, the Offeror must have a current/valid registration in the Systems for Award Management (SAM) database website: www.sam.gov. Registration must be active by the offer due date. Proposals must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 3:00 pm ET on September 10, 2026. Please see attached SIR for proposal submission requirements. Questions are to be submitted, in writing, as specified in the SIR. Please reference the SIR number and BEYOND Phase 2 program on all question submissions. All questions must be received no later than 1:00pm ET on September 3, 2026. Questions will be answered in an Amendment to the SIR if deemed necessary and posted to SAM.GOV for all interested parties to consider. Prospective Offerors are encouraged to frequently visit SAM.GOV for any updates to this requirement. Any questions regarding this announcement should be directed to Kristin Frantz, Contracting Officer, at Kristin.T.Frantz@faa.gov and Jackson LeMay, Contract Specialist, at Jackson.T.Lemay@faa.gov Any proposals received after the closing date and time, will not be considered in accordance with this SIR. This SIR is not to be construed as a contract or a commitment of any kind. The Government will not be liable for payment of any costs attributed to the preparation and submission of requested proposal documentation.

title: Modernization of Scientific and Technical Intelligence (SandTI;) Prototype Effort

description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE Product Service Code: DA01 � IT and Telecom � BUSINESS APPLICATION/APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT SERVICES (LABOR) NAICS Code: 541519 � Other Computer Related Services Solicitation Number: W50NH9-26-R-A019 Notice Type: Pre-Solicitation Procuring Agency: U.S. Army Contracting Command � Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) Requiring Activity: U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM) Anticipated Award Type: Time and Materials (T&M), 5-Year Long-Term Contract (LTC) The United States Army Contracting Command � Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA), on behalf of the U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM), intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) W50NH9-26-R-A019 for Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Architecture Information Technology (IT) Contractor Manpower Equivalent (CME) Support (formerly known as Integrated Geospatial Intelligence Enterprise Architecture - IGEA). This action involved holistic IT services and related logistic, programmatic, training, and management support for GEOINT operations. The planned level of effort is 30 Full-time Equivalents (FTEs), plus up to an additional three surge FTEs, distributed across various Contiguous United States (CONUS) and Outside the Contiguous United States (OCONUS). Most of the performance is expected to occur at Fort Gordon, Georgia, but other locations include Honolulu, Hawaii; Wiesbaden, Germany; Vicenza, Italy; Republic of Korea; San Antonio, Texas; and Colorado Springs, Colorado. title: 2027 Southern Hemisphere Influenza Vaccine
description: The Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support is soliciting for the supply of Southern Hemisphere Influenza Vaccine for the 2027-2028 flu season. Approximately 30,000 doses are included in this requirement. (Quantities may increase or decrease pending receipt of final Service requirements.) The vaccines shall be a pre-measured 0.5 ML dose, each dose shall be pre-filled in a commercially available syringe for intramuscular administration in healthy individuals aged 6 months and older. The vaccine shall be U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA)-approved and U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommended. The formula for the 2027-2028 season vaccine shall be determined by the FDA�s Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee. Other specification data is included in the solicitation. Successful contractor must have FDA Approval and the vaccine must be ACIP recommended. National Stock Numbers shall be established at time of award. An indefinite quantity contract is proposed. The quantity indicated is an annual estimate only. (Quantities may increase or decrease pending receipt of final Service requirements.) The guaranteed minimum will be 75% of the annual estimate, and a contract maximum will be established at 150% of the annual estimate. All quantities shall be delivered to the Defense Depot New Cumberland, PA. The contractor shall be capable of delivering 100% of the requirements by March 12, 2027. This delivery schedule is the preferred delivery schedule. Other delivery schedules will be considered. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and SAM.gov at https://www.sam.gov. Interested parties should contact Rosbert Jones (rosbert.jones@dla.mil) for any questions/comments. Interested parties are further advised to set up automated notifications of presolicitation or solicitation changes through this website. The current projected solicitation date is September 28, 2026, closing on Ocrtober 14, 2026. DLA reserves the right to issue the solicitation before or after the projected solicitation date.

When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. title: Finland – Translation services – Viittomakielisten tulkkausten ja käännösten hankinta valtioneuvostolle
description: Valtioneuvoston kanslia (VNK) on yksi 12 ministeriöstä. Sen päätehtävä on tukea pääministeriä valtioneuvoston johtamisessa sekä hallituksen ja eduskunnan työn yhteensovittamisessa. VNK vastaa valtioneuvoston toiminnan organisoinnista ja hallituksen toimintaedellytysten järjestämisestä kaikissa olosuhteissa. Hankinnan kohteena ovat valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden tarvitsemien suomalaisen ja suomenruotsalaisen viittomakielen tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluiden hankinta. Tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluita tarvitaan pääsääntöisesti suomesta ja/tai ruotsista suomalaiselle ja suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle, mutta jonkin verran myös suomalaisesta ja suomenruotsalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi. Viittomakielisiä tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluita tarvitaan erityisesti 1.7.2026 valtioneuvoston kansliassa aloittaneen valtioneuvoston viestintäosaston tarpeisiin. Valtioneuvoston viestintäosasto vastaa valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden viestinnästä ja valtionhallinnon viestinnän yhteensovittamisesta. Suositus viittomakielten käytöstä valtioneuvoston viestinnässä 2025 edistää viittomakielisten kielellisten oikeuksien toteutumista. Viestintään liittyvien tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluiden lisäksi hankinnan kohteena ovat myös ministeriöiden muut viittomakieliset tulkkaus- ja käännöstarpeet (osa-alueet 5-8), joiden hankinnassa valtioneuvoston kanslia toimii hankintarenkaan vetäjänä ja hankintarenkaassa ovat mukana liikenne- ja viestintäministeriö, oikeusministeriö, opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö, sosiaali- ja terveysministeriö, ulkoministeriö ja valtiovarainministeriö sekä oikeuskanslerinvirasto. Tulkkaukset ja käännökset voivat koskea mitä tahansa ministeriöiden toimialoihin kuuluvaa asiaa, ks. valtioneuvoston ohjesääntö 262/2003, § 10–24, https://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/ajantasa/2003/20030262. Lisätietoa ministeriöiden toiminnasta on saatavilla ministeriöiden www-sivustoilla, ks. https://valtioneuvosto.fi/ministeriot Hankinta on EU-kynnysarvon ylittävä palveluhankinta ja se on jaettu kahdeksaan osa-alueeseen: 1. Tiedotustilaisuuksien tulkkaukset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle 2. Tiedotustilaisuuksien tulkkaukset suomesta ja ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle 3. Viestintään liittyvät käännökset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle 4. Viestintään liittyvät käännökset ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle 5. Muut tulkkaukset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle ja suomalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi 6. Muut tulkkaukset suomesta ja ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle ja suomenruotsalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi ja ruotsiksi 7. title: Industry Day U.S. Merchant Marine Academy Campus Modernization
description: FALL FY27 INDUSTRY DAY U.S. Merchant Marine Academy Campus Modernization Industry Day Special Notice | Thursday, October 15, 2026 Event Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), New York District, and the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy (USMMA) will host the Fall FY27 Industry Day from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 15, 2026. The hybrid event will bring industry, government, community organizations, and other interested attendees together with USMMA and USACE leadership for an updated view of the Campus Modernization Initiative, its strategic direction, and anticipated procurement activity. This event is open to the general public, and interested vendors. The FY27-FY28 forecast will emphasize the substantial heavy construction opportunities central to the modernization program while also addressing utility upgrades and complementary supporting and non-construction requirements. In-person participation is strongly encouraged. Prior registration is required for every attendee and closes at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 12, 2026. Event Information Event: USMMA Campus Modernization Fall FY27 Industry Day Date: Thursday, October 15, 2026 Event Time: 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time Check-In: Opens at 10:00 a.m.; in-person attendees should arrive no later than 10:45 a.m. to allow at least 15 minutes for networking before the program begins Location: U.S. Merchant Marine Academy, 300 Steamboat Road, Kings Point, NY 11024; enter through the main gate Format: Hybrid; in-person attendance is strongly encouraged. Registered virtual attendees will receive a Microsoft Teams link on October 13, 2026 Audience: All interested attendees age 16 or older (public attendees welcome) Registration Deadline: 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday, October 12, 2026 Theme: USACE Partnering with Industry and the Local Community Industry Day Highlights The Industry Day program will include the following: Welcome and Keynote Remarks: USACE leadership, USMMA Academy leadership, and invited guests will discuss the modernization program, acquisition approaches, and community impacts. Strategic Program Overview: A general USMMA overview and FY27-FY28 Campus Modernization update, including the strategic vision, updated waterfall chart, and local-government and community considerations. Heavy Construction Forecast: A focused review of the significant heavy construction opportunities expected to drive the modernization program. Specific project names, dollar ranges, and acquisition methods will be presented at the event rather than released in this notice. Supporting and Utility Requirements: Discussion of utility upgrades and complementary non-construction requirements that support successful delivery of the broader construction program. Executive Panel and Q&A: A moderator-led discussion with USMMA leadership, USACE program representatives, and USACE Contracting, including questions and topics submitted by industry. Doing Business with the Government: A practical session presented by the USACE Office of Small Business Programs. Campus Tour and Networking: A campus tour and opportunities to engage with program managers, technical staff, government representatives, community stakeholders, and industry peers. Advance Industry Questions: Industry partners may submit proposed questions or discussion topics for the executive panel to Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil no later than September 30, 2026. Registration and Access Information Registration is required for every attendee, regardless of affiliation or attendance method. Email the information below to Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil no later than 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Monday, October 12, 2026. Use the subject line "USMMA FY27 Industry Day Registration." One representative may register multiple attendees, but the required information must be provided separately for each person. Full legal name of each attendee Organization, company, or other affiliation, if applicable Individual email address and telephone number for each attendee Attendance method: in person or virtual Company website, if applicable Current capability statement for industry participants Virtual Attendance: A Microsoft Teams link will be emailed to registered virtual attendees on October 13, 2026. In-person attendance is strongly encouraged. Campus Access Requirements All in-person attendees must present a valid REAL ID-compliant credential or another form of government-issued photo identification acceptable to USMMA security and comply with all campus-entry instructions provided to registered attendees. Logistics and Parking Campus Entrance: Use the main gate at 300 Steamboat Road, Kings Point, NY 11024. Parking: Free attendee parking is available in Marvin Lot; overnight parking is not permitted. Arrival: Check-in opens at 10:00 a.m. Allow time to enter, park, and walk to the event location; arrive no later than 10:45 a.m. for networking. On-Site Directions: Follow posted signs and directions from USMMA security and event personnel. Updates, Changes, and Cancellations Any material change to the schedule, format, access procedures, or event status will be announced through an amendment to this SAM.gov notice and by email to registered attendees. Notice Status and Disclaimer This announcement is for informational and advance-planning purposes only and is not a solicitation or Government commitment to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse costs associated with this notice or event. Attendance is not required to participate in a future acquisition, and all event information is subject to change. Primary Point of Contact Name: Zachery A. Bernard Title: Deputy, Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) Organization: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, North Atlantic Division - New York District Email: Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil Registration Email Subject: USMMA FY27 Industry Day Registration END OF SPECIAL NOTICE

description: 12 August Amendment 02 to revise documents as a result of Q&A. 28 Jul 26 Amendment 01 to revised documents as a result of Q&A. 10 Jul 26 Center Console Refresh addresses critical obsolescence issues within the KC-135 Refueling Tanker aircraft. The US Air Force needs an updated Fuel System (FS), Flight Display System (FDS), and Flight Computer due to obsolescence and is looking for innovative ideas to not only replace but improve these systems with turn-key solutions enabling supportability and future growth. The FS, FDS, Flight Computer, and the future growth/adaptability define the scope of the CCR program. The program scope also includes the addition of autothrottle systems. The anticipated contract will be a Cost-Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF) for EMD, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) for Production and Deployment (P&D), single award indefinite delivery/quantity type contract comprised of One (1) 48-month Base Period with Six (6) 1-Year Option Periods and a projected period of performance from July 2028 to June 2038.
